summary: Tested the new Notification & Alert system end-to-end. Backend (REST + WebSocket) fully passes 6/6 pytest cases. Frontend passes all critical flows: bell icon on both Book and My Bookings tabs, live toast banners (variants brand/info/success) via WebSocket, unread badge with numeric count, navigation to /notifications, mark-all-read on open, CLEAR button, and empty state. WebSocket /api/ws/notifications correctly delivers real-time events with event='notification'.

ui_bugs.issue: When a toast is on screen (up to ~4.2s), it visually overlaps the header on small viewports (375x667) and its inner children have full pointerEvents; a tap that lands on the toast area does NOT reach the underlying bell icon. On the first UI test (375x667) tapping the bell while a fresh toast was visible did not navigate to /notifications. Once the toast animated away the same tap worked. Consider raising the bell's z-index above ToastHost, or making toast items intercept-safe (e.g. wrap items in pointerEvents='box-none' when they don't need input, or reduce the toast width to leave the bell tap area free).

issues: Console warning: 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents'. In /app/frontend/src/components/ToastHost.tsx line 48 <View pointerEvents="box-none"> — move to style.pointerEvents to silence the deprecation warning on RN Web/newer RN.

react_native_issues.issue: Uses deprecated `pointerEvents` prop instead of `style.pointerEvents`. Reference: /app/frontend/src/components/ToastHost.tsx:48 (and the Platform.OS==='web' spread at line 107 also sets it as a style — the prop form on line 48 is the deprecated one).

action_items: Fix ToastHost overlap over BellIcon: elevate BellIcon zIndex above the toast host, or constrain toast width / add extra top offset so tapping the header bell isn't intercepted while a toast is animating.
Migrate `pointerEvents="box-none"` to `style={{ pointerEvents: 'box-none' }}` on the ToastHost root View (/app/frontend/src/components/ToastHost.tsx:48) to remove the RN deprecation warning.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 582 lines — still under 700, but approaching the split threshold; consider moving Notifications into its own module.
Backend correctly excludes MongoDB _id in all responses (find({}, {'_id': 0}) and doc.pop('_id') after insert).
Frontend correctly uses process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL (via src/lib/api.ts) — no hardcoded URLs.
NotificationsProvider has WebSocket auto-reconnect with 3s backoff and refreshes state on reconnect — good.
All interactive elements have testID (bell-icon, bell-badge, clear-all-button, back-button, notif-<id>, notifications-empty, toast-<variant>).

success_rate.frontend: 100% functional (7/7 UI cases; 1 timing-related overlap issue reproducible but not blocking flow)

seed_data_creation: Bookings are created via API during tests using 'Andheri West, Mumbai' → 'Bandra West, Mumbai' and are cleaned by DELETE /api/notifications at start & end of each test module. Bookings themselves are not deleted (no DELETE booking endpoint), but they don't interfere with subsequent runs.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The Notifications system is fully working. Backend: /api/notifications (GET, POST /read-all, DELETE) + /api/ws/notifications. Frontend: NotificationsProvider mounted in _layout.tsx, BellIcon on both tab headers, ToastHost overlay. Reuse /app/backend/tests/test_notifications.py for regression. Known cosmetic issue: toast overlays bell for ~4s which can intercept taps on small viewports.
rca_of_issue: For the intermittent bell-tap failure: ToastHost is rendered AFTER the Stack in _layout.tsx at absolute position top:0. Individual toast Animated.Views have default pointerEvents='auto'. Because the toast container spans the full width (paddingHorizontal:12 only), a toast covers the bell area at the top-right for ~4.2s. Mitigation: either (a) set style={{ pointerEvents: 'box-none' }} on Animated.View items so only the close-button captures events, or (b) raise BellIcon zIndex/elevation above the toast host, or (c) render ToastHost BEFORE the Stack so it sits underneath the header.
